name: IL-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Budzinski's massive financial advantage ($2.6M cash vs. $12K for Wilson)
District's Democratic lean (D+5 PVI) plus incumbent advantage
No public polling or expert ratings to refine the estimate
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Budzinski: a D+5 district, incumbency, a favorable national environment, and a lopsided money edge over Wilson, whose campaign has just $12K on hand. Markets agree, pricing her near 96%, so the forecast stays in Safe D territory with a modest trim for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or a polling surprise showing Wilson competitive would be the first sign this race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term Democrat Nikki Budzinski seeks reelection in an Illinois district that leans Democratic by about five points. She enters the general election with a dominant financial position, having raised nearly $2.9 million and holding $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Jeff Wilson has raised about $348,000 and reports only $12,000 in the bank. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Budzinski roughly a 96% chance of winning. The forecast places her comfortably ahead, though the lack of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
